1813-02-01.summary: Lee attacks Warden's assumption of charge of the legation after Barlow's death: in cipher, the intrigues of the Irish Brigade and Marshal Sérurier on Warden's behalf, his use of Barlow's letter to Latrobe, toasts to the success of Clinton and Emmet, and his claim that the United Irishmen form a party so strong in the United States that the President dares not offend them.
1813-02-01.en:
The letter is in Lee's hand, dated from the Hotel of the Legation in Paris and marked private. It runs to seven
pages, nearly all in clear, with eight short passages in his cipher. No decipherment by the State Department clerk
was found on the film. The whole letter is given here, with the docket. It
is not the letter of the same date, wholly in clear, in which Lee regrets that he has not the cipher.

Lee's clear text is plain. Words he wrote in cipher are in italics. Bold italics mark cipher that the clerk who read
these letters at the State Department did not read. A dagger † after a passage means the clerk failed or left a gap
there. The sign ≠ means his wording differs from what the cipher gives. A double dagger ‡ means he never came to it.
The sign § means that our reading rests on a slip we suppose Lee made with his key, or on a doubtful division of
the figures: it is a proposal.

1813-02-02.summary: Barlow's treaty is to go before Napoleon, who would sanction it except for the indemnities the United States demands; France will spin out the negotiations and offer commercial advantages instead; Lee cites Barlow's correspondence with the Dukes of Bassano and Dalberg and cannot send a copy of the treaty.
1813-02-02.en:
The letter was deciphered at the State Department in 1813 on separate sheets, and the printed edition gives that
copy with the clerk's notes of error. Our reading is made from the figures, not from his copy. It agrees with him
wherever he read a passage, except where marked, and it reads seven passages that he could not.

1813-02-06.summary: France after the Russian disaster: the Grand Army destroyed, discontent, conscription and forced donations as the last effort of the nation, Austria's armed neutrality and possible mediation, Prussia's king fleeing the Russians, terms of peace offered to England if she abandons Russia, and Napoleon's hopes resting on the coming campaign. The last 32 stretches carry no decipherment on this copy, and none was found.
1813-02-06.en:
No full decipherment of the letter was found. The clerk at the State Department wrote the letters of the key over
the figures and his reading under them in pencil on the first three pages, and stopped on the third. The last
thirty-two passages carry no decipherment on this copy (it is headed "Second Copy"; no other copy was looked for).

system: Vigenère-type cipher with numerals 1-25 for ciphertext over the alphabet ABCDEFGHIKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ (I/J one letter), keyword WINCHESTER: plaintext index = (numeral - 1 + index of the key letter) mod 25, the key restarted at W for each coded stretch. Only…
